headline: 17-Year-Old Builds Supply Network Based on Anonymity, Not Shame
meta_description: Vivian Ho, 17, founded All The Same Organization to deliver supplies to low-income families without requiring them to identify themselves as needing help.
summary_short: A Texas teenager realized that asking people to declare their need was itself a barrier to help. So she built a national organization around anonymous requests.
body:
At 17, Vivian Ho recognized a fundamental problem with how most social programs work: they ask people to publicly identify themselves as needing help before delivering it. This moment of exposure, she realized, was often what kept people from asking at all. So she built All The Same Organization around a different premise—that dignity means never having to name yourself as someone in need.

ATS operates through Title I schools across the country, delivering food, hygiene products, school supplies, and household necessities. Families request what they needs through an anonymous sign-up system, and volunteers pack boxes without ever knowing the recipient's identity. The organization has grown to more than 200 chapters with roughly 8,000 volunteers and has distributed over 150,000 supplies since its founding. In a single back-to-school season alone, ATS served five schools and delivered more than 15,000 school supplies.

What distinguishes Ho's work is how intentionally she considers the human experience beyond logistics. Her Cultural Surprises program asks volunteers to research a recipient family's background and create handmade crafts based on their culture—more than 500 crafts have been made for over 60 recipients. The program emerged from Ho's own experience as a Vietnamese immigrant who suppressed her cultural identity growing up. Now she recognizes that students in Title I schools often do the same. A new Cultural Spotlight Scholarship invites students to create art inspired by their own cultures, with winners receiving $1,250 and their work shared with a wider audience.

When Ho's initial medical classroom project at Dobie Middle School was shut down during a school turnaround, she simply redirected her efforts to other schools. Her co-founder noted that Ho's willingness to keep finding ways to help, even when original plans failed, reflects her core belief: people should be able to ask for help without giving anything of themselves away to get it.
quick_facts: 17-year-old Vivian Ho founded All The Same Organization in Cedar Park, Texas
Over 200 chapters nationwide with 8,000 volunteers and 150,000+ supplies distributed
Anonymous sign-up system allows families to request help without identifying themselves
Cultural Surprises program creates handmade crafts reflecting recipient families' backgrounds
15,000 school supplies delivered in a single back-to-school season
